prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single, objectively “best” agent for every seller — the right one depends on your goals (maximum price vs fastest sale vs low hassle), your neighborhood and price range, and the working style you prefer. I can help you find the best agent for you. Here’s a practical plan and what to look for.

Quick plan to find the right Pleasanton agent
1. Narrow candidates to 3–5 local agents who recently sold similar homes in your neighborhood and price range (look for sales in the last 6–12 months).  
2. Check their track record (days on market, list price vs sale price, number of similar comps).  
3. Interview each agent (in person or Zoom). Use the same set of questions so you can compare.  
4. Ask for a custom CMA (comparable market analysis), a marketing plan, and a net-proceeds estimate.  
5. Compare fees, services, staging/photography plans and references, then choose the agent you trust.

Where to find candidates
- Local MLS results (best source for who’s selling homes in Pleasanton).  
- Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com: look at agents listed on recent sold listings.  
- Google and Yelp reviews, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups for referrals.  
- Major brokerages active in Pleasanton (Keller Williams, Compass, Coldwell Banker, Berkshire Hathaway, etc.) — check their local top producers.

Key metrics to ask for and compare
- How many Pleasanton homes like yours have they sold in the past 12 months?  
- Average days on market and list-price to sale-price ratio for those sales.  
- Number of buyer leads generated per listing (open houses, online marketing, buyer database).  
- Their commission and what services are included (staging, pro photos, floor plans, virtual tours, paid ads).  
- References from 2–3 recent Pleasanton sellers and permission to contact them.

Interview questions (use these with each agent)
- What is your recommended list price and why? Show the comparable sales.  
- What is your marketing plan for my home (online, social, broker outreach, staging)?  
- How will you target likely buyers for my neighborhood/price point?  
- What are your recent comparable sales in Pleasanton? Can I see final closing data?  
- What’s your negotiation strategy if we receive multiple offers or low offers?  
- What is your fee/commission and any additional costs? Can we itemize expected closing costs?  
- Who will be my day-to-day contact (you or an assistant)? How often will I get updates?  
- Can you provide client references and recent seller results?

Red flags
- Agent can’t or won’t provide recent comparable sales or a clear marketing plan.  
- Very vague answers about pricing strategy or how they handle negotiations.  
- No online presence or poor-quality listing photos for their recent listings.  
- Pressure to sign an exclusive listing agreement immediately without a CMA.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short message you can send to 3–5 agents asking for their CMA and marketing plan.  
- Create an interview-score sheet to compare agents side-by-side.  
- If you share the property address, target price, and timeline, I can suggest specific things to look for in the CMAs you receive.

Which of those would be most helpful right now?
